bioAdditions: The 1900 census, taken on 7 June 1900 in the East Division of Plymouth Township, gives Addison's birth as December 1867, matching the FamilySearch tree and supporting 1867 over the 1868 in his obituary (S1). He was a carpenter, married seven years, and owned his house subject to a mortgage. The family group around him is striking: in the next dwelling lived his brother Orange Pringle (b. June 1870, a coal-breaker laborer) with their mother Catherine, recorded as 'Mother', divorced, born in May 1835 or 1838 (the last digit is unclear), mother of seven children of whom five were living; and one dwelling further on lived Ella Randal, a widow born August 1860, with her children Fred and Gertrude, very probably Addison's sister Ellen (Pringle) Randall (S1). Three of Andrew G. Pringle's children and his former wife were thus living side by side in 1900.

conflicts.assessment: Ages conflict across records: 1870 census age 5 (c.1865) and 1880 age 15 (c.1865) vs 1900 Dec 1867 vs obituary 2 Dec 1868. December is consistent; the year is 1865-68. The 1870/1880 ages were given while he was a child in his parents' household and may be more reliable than later self-reports; the 1943 death certificate is needed.

openQuestionsResolved.question: Why Bradsby (1893) omitted him from his mother's living children.
openQuestionsResolved.answer: Not resolved directly, but the 1900 census shows he lived next door to his mother, so estrangement is unlikely; the omission is probably an error in the family-supplied sketch. In 1900 she reported 7 children born, 5 living, which matches Bradsby's 'five living' only if one of Bradsby's five was counted differently - Addison was certainly living.
